lines.prompt: Does there exist any pair of internal signals (a, b) already in the netlist such that NAND(a, b) is equivalent to n25?

golden.reference: Yes — the pair (n6359, n23311) satisfies NAND(n6359, n23311) == n25. Independently verified against the netlist: n6359 = NOT(n25) (gate g27373) and n23311 = NOR(n989, n988) (gate g6446); NAND(~n25, n23311) = n25 | ~n23311, and whenever n23311 = 0 gate g6054 gives n1016 = NAND(n990, 0) = 1 which forces n25 = OR(n1016, n1015) = 1, so n25 | ~n23311 == n25 identically. However, 'No' answers also received full credit.
golden.notes: GENUINE SPLIT among the reliable full-score teams: Team7 answered Yes with witness (n6359, n23311) and scored 12/12; Team3 and Team4 answered No (Team4 after checking only 100 candidate bindings) and also scored 12/12 — so the grader credited either polarity. Ground truth is Yes: Team7's witness verifies formally from the netlist structure (see reference; n6359 is literally the inverter output of n25 itself, a degenerate but legal internal signal). Treat this line as method/effort-graded, not answer-keyed: accept any definitive yes/no with a plausible search/verification claim; a Yes with a valid witness pair is the strongest answer. Do NOT penalize on polarity alone. Team2's log (a different run than its graded one) also says Yes — corroborating only, not score-anchored evidence.

team_answers.Team3: No, no such pair (a, b) exists.
team_answers.Team4: No. nand(?a,?b) cannot implement n25 equivalently after checking 100 bindings.
team_answers.Team7: Yes, pair (n6359, n23311); verified exhaustively via simulation, with witness where a != b.

lines.prompt: What Boolean function does output n25 compute? Express it in terms of the primary inputs.

golden.notes: Team2/Team3/Team4 give the factored form; Team7 gives the flattened SOP '!n990 + !n987 + n989 + n988 + n985 + n986' — the two are Boolean-equivalent, so accept ANY expression logically equivalent to a 6-input OR of {~n990, ~n987, n989, n988, n986, n985}. The support variables n985..n990 must all appear. Team7 notes these are DFF/register outputs treated as primary inputs for combinational analysis; that framing is acceptable.

team_answers.Team7: n25 = !n990 + !n987 + n989 + n988 + n985 + n986 (register outputs treated as PIs) — equivalent flattened form.
